A source guide for a deeper dive.This entry provides a brief orientation and an organized reading path. A comprehensive deep dive has not yet been completed. Follow the annotated sources and distinguish primary community accounts from outside reference material.
01

Identity and context

The Cree Nation of Eeyou Istchee identifies its people as Eeyou and locates its homeland primarily in northern Québec, with historically occupied lands in Ontario. Its community account emphasizes distinct local histories alongside shared connections and describes local governments working through regional institutions.

Read the sources [1] Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

02

A path for deeper reading

Start with this government's own community descriptions and follow its links to individual First Nations. Research beyond Eeyou Istchee is still needed before this guide can represent the wider range of Cree communities and languages.

Read the sources [1] Grand Council of the Crees (Eeyou Istchee) / Cree Nation Government

What needs further research

  • The old Cow Creek Umpqua publication is unrelated to Cree and should be replaced, not relabelled.
  • The source distinguishes local First Nations and an Eeyou regional government; these are not a single government for all Cree people.
  • No census counts, area totals, current officers, present treaty membership or current legal conclusions are asserted.
  • Keep the broader entry name Cree and kind Wider grouping / peoples. This is a limited starter reading path, not a proposed renaming of all Cree as Eeyou.
  • Do not add unrelated Plains Cree, Nêhiyaw or other regional assertions from this one page. No map data or canonical source was edited.

The Eeyou of Eeyou Istchee ↗

The Cree government's community account connects Eeyou identity, northern Québec homeland, historical Ontario lands and distinct local histories. Read the introduction, governance paragraphs and community descriptions. Scope is Eeyou Istchee, not every Cree people or language. Undated totals, officeholders and treaty-process statements are not adopted as current.
